research_question: Among older adults with hypertension, what is the effect of assignment to a higher blood pressure target (approximately systolic/diastolic 150–160/95–100 mmHg; the less intensively treated arm) versus a lower blood pressure target (approximately 140/90 mmHg; the more intensively treated arm) on all-cause mortality?
treatment_label: Higher blood pressure target (approximately 150–160/95–100 mmHg; less intensive treatment), matched to each trial’s higher-target arm
control_label: Lower blood pressure target (approximately 140/90 mmHg; more intensive treatment), matched to each trial’s lower-target arm
outcome_description: Single dichotomous outcome: all-cause mortality (death from any cause), using the reported number of deaths and total randomized in each arm. Cardiovascular mortality, non-cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and all other outcomes are outside this analysis.
positive_direction: A positive standardized effect, if one were calculated, would indicate lower all-cause mortality and therefore favor the higher-BP-target treatment arm; for the requested pooled risk ratio, RR < 1 favors the higher-target arm and RR > 1 favors the lower-target arm.
search_queries: older adults hypertension higher versus lower blood pressure target randomized trial mortality
elderly hypertension blood pressure treatment target controlled trial deaths
less intensive versus intensive blood pressure target older adults all-cause mortality trial
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical comparative studies of older adults with hypertension assigned to higher versus lower blood pressure treatment targets broadly corresponding to the target ranges of interest.
Studies reporting all-cause mortality as deaths and randomized totals by treatment-target arm, or equivalent quantitative information from which a risk ratio can be derived.
Any publication status, setting, language, or follow-up duration, provided the treatment-target comparison and usable mortality data are available.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, commentaries, guidelines, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between a higher blood pressure target treatment arm and a lower blood pressure target control arm.

No quantitative all-cause mortality outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as arm-level deaths with denominators, proportions, odds ratios, or other convertible statistics; means with SDs or t/F-values alone are not sufficient for this dichotomous outcome.
Completely unrelated to blood pressure treatment targets in older adults with hypertension.
moderators_to_extract: Mean or median participant age and minimum age eligibility
Exact systolic and diastolic targets assigned in each arm
Baseline cardiovascular risk or comorbidity burden
effect_size_note: Pool arm-level all-cause mortality as a risk ratio (RR) using deaths and total randomized per arm, preserving intention-to-treat denominators where reported. Code each trial’s higher-target group as treatment and lower-target group as control based on the trial’s assigned targets, never on treatment intensity; the higher target is generally the less intensively treated arm. RR < 1 indicates fewer deaths with the higher target. Keep all-cause mortality separate from cause-specific mortality and other outcomes. Record handling of zero-event arms and avoid double-counting overlapping reports or shared comparator groups.
